samples.title: Pedestrians on a campus path (OpenCV sample clip)
samples.source: samples/data/vtest.avi in the OpenCV repository (https://github.com/opencv/opencv). Re-encoded to H.264 without other changes.
samples.licence: Distributed in the Apache-2.0 licensed OpenCV repository as a sample file for its video examples. The repository does not document who recorded it; no other rights or consents are claimed.
samples.contains: Several people walking along a path, filmed from a fixed elevated camera. It is NOT a restaurant.
demonstrates: drawing a monitored area and getting entry, exit and duration events
incomplete observations when a track starts or ends inside the area
the attendance comparison workflow (with a fictional schedule)

samples.title: Table tennis composite test clip (rendered table and ball, real-pixel people)
samples.source: Generated by services/video-intel/scripts/make_samples.py. The table, net and ball are rendered with a known camera; the two people are cut-outs of walkers from the OpenCV pedestrian clip. Ground truth (ball path, rallies, table corners) is in table-tennis-composite.truth.json.
samples.licence: Generated by Neo Forge Technology. The person cut-outs derive from the Apache-2.0 licensed OpenCV sample clip; no other rights or consents are claimed.
samples.contains: Three rendered rallies (5, 7 and 4 strokes) separated by pauses in which the ball is not visible.
demonstrates: ball tracking with gaps marked as gaps, measured against the known ball path
table calibration from four clicked corners and a measurable reprojection error
ball-visible segments, bounce and net-side-crossing candidates
does_not_demonstrate: accuracy on real video with motion blur and clutter

samples.title: Basketball composite test clip (rendered court and ball, real-pixel people)
samples.source: Generated by services/video-intel/scripts/make_samples.py. The court lines and ball are rendered with a known camera; four people are cut-outs of walkers from the OpenCV pedestrian clip moving on known paths. Ground truth (ball path, possession intervals, court corners) is in basketball-composite.truth.json.
samples.licence: Generated by Neo Forge Technology. The person cut-outs derive from the Apache-2.0 licensed OpenCV sample clip; no other rights or consents are claimed.
samples.contains: A ball dribbled and passed between four players in the right half-court.
demonstrates: court mapping from manual reference points and the resulting error in metres
heat map and distance from real tracks
Potential Possession Events against the known holding intervals
orange-ball tracking against the known ball path
